Jordan / Monica — internal note before I send to Acme: 

Summary of what I’ll prepare:
- redwood-subprocessor-inventory-2026-09.pdf (approved list; marks processors used for hosting, telemetry, monitoring)
- sample-audit-logs-export-stub.txt (10k rows, redacted PII, shows timestamps, request_id, model, route, region)
- short technical note: EU customer traffic stays within EU regions by default; failover routing to US occurs only if EU capacity unavailable and only to FIPS-compliant nodes. Transfer mechanism: Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) with optional DP addendum — see DocuSign link I’ll reference.

Questions for Privacy: 
1) Do we proactively share full Art.30 records or only a summary? Acme’s DPIA template asks for processing records per Article 30.
2) Any objections to providing a redacted sample of the events log (we strip request body tokens and replace user identifiers with hashed ids)?

I’ll attach the PDFs and the stub here in the outgoing reply.

-Karthik
Senior Reliability Engineer (Infra Compliance)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Nadia Alvi <nadia.alvi@acmehealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 14:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Cross-border DPIA evidence & audit-rights coordination

Hi Nadia — thank you, and nice to meet you virtually. I spoke with Legal to confirm scope. High-level responses below and next steps: 

1) Subprocessor inventory: attached (redwood-subprocessor-inventory-2026-09.pdf). This includes vendor categories and subprocessors used for hosted and telemetry services.

2) Art. 28 / 30 materials: we do not share full internal Art.30 registers as-is, but we can provide a concise processing activity summary compatible with Article 30 requirements (purpose, categories of data, categories of recipients, retention). Please see the attached one-page summary.

3) Audit logs & sample export: we can provide a redacted sample export (attached: sample-audit-logs-export-stub.txt). The sample will have all PII redacted and user identifiers hashed; it shows timestamps, request_id, model, and region. For full audit access requests, we require an executed audit agreement and a minimal scope statement — procurement usually prefers a remote evidence review rather than direct DB access.

4) Cross-border transfer mechanics: For EU accounts, data is served from EU regions by default. Failover to US nodes happens only under capacity/incident conditions and is covered by SCCs and our DPA transfer clause. We can include a written attestation and DocuSign of SCC inclusion.

Deliverables we will send by Tue 2026-09-15 if not sooner: 
- redwood-subprocessor-inventory-2026-09.pdf
- Processing_activities_summary_Art30.txt
- sample-audit-logs-export-stub.txt
- DocuSign link for SCC confirmation (if requested)

If procurement needs an expedited full-scope remote audit, please provide the preferred week and the scope (systems / date range). Otherwise the attached material should be suitable for Acme’s DPIA.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Privacy & Compliance Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-subprocessor-inventory-2026-09.pdf (pdf), Processing_activities_summary_Art30.txt (txt), sample-audit-logs-export-stub.txt (txt)

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Nadia
